thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: inference-qps-exceed-slo (pd://P12345) — 98% of requests to /v1/embeddings are > 300ms p50. Trigger threshold breached by traffic split for release v3.4.0-canary.

tyler (on-call): saw it, I'm taking. first look — hitting higher CPU on the embedding workers.

maria (eng-sre): heading in. can we confirm if this is canary only or traffic split leak?

sam (eng-runtime): quick note: v3.4.0 changed the kv-cache behavior (prefetch enabled) and we saw a kernel fallback for quantized paths on the embeddings container in canary. Might be increasing token-encode latency under high QPS.

tyler (on-call): ok. @sam can you grep logs for kv cache errors? I'll open a quick smoke on prod-canary.

sam (eng-runtime): logs snippet: ```
2026-03-05T14:02:11Z serve-emb-0 kernel: fallback_to_f32: model=embed-2048q, shard=2, reason=unsupported-quant-kernel
2026-03-05T14:02:12Z serve-emb-0 runtime: kv_cache_prefetch: 12ms -> 85ms
```

tyler (on-call): confirmed. canary hosts show 4-5x p50 increase vs baseline. traffic split currently 15% canary.

jamie (product): customer impact? any 5xxs or just latency? we already have a few support tickets flagged 'slow embeddings'.

maria (eng-sre): no 5xx spike, only latency. user-facing features (search/semantic match) degraded for some customers. I'm pulling top impacted org ids.

tyler (on-call): immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce canary traffic to 0% 2) if latency doesn't drop in 90s, rollback canary 3) if rollback blocked, scale up embeddings pool. I'll execute step 1 now.

sam (eng-runtime): quick command to set split: ```sh
# set traffic split to 0% for canary
redwoodctl rollout traffic-set --service=embedding-service --from=v3.4.0-canary --to=stable --percent=0
```

tyler (on-call): ran the traffic-set command. pd link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/P12345.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Automation: traffic-set job completed (job-id: ts-9987).

tyler (on-call): p50 dropped from 320ms -> 120ms within 2 minutes. Good signal.

maria (eng-sre): monitoring shows p50 settling at ~110ms, p95 trending down. No new errors. I'll update the incident severity to SEV-2 (no customer outages, degraded perf).

sam (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: new prefetch path triggers a quantization kernel fallback for some model shards under certain batch sizes — increases CPU + memory copy. We'll need perf patch or revert kv-prefetch.

jamie (product): thanks for fast mitigation. Are we rolling back or reverting the feature for stable?

sam (eng-runtime): two options: quick rollback of the canary (undo rollout) or patch runtime to guard quant kernel selection. rollback is lowest risk short-term.

tyler (on-call): I think we should rollback canary entirely to be safe. I'm going to do a canary rollback and then schedule a follow-up for a codefix.

rachael (next-oncall): I'm on standby to take over the follow-up after 16:00 UTC. If you need continuous monitoring, I can join.

tyler (on-call): executing rollback: ```sh
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/embedding-service --to-revision=stable
redwoodctl rollout status --service=embedding-service --timeout=5m
```

incident-bot: :information_source: Deployment event: rollback initiated by tyler (job-id: rb-4412).

sam (eng-runtime): watching logs, new pods come up with stable image, quant kernel selection back to optimized path.

maria (eng-sre): p50 back to 70-90ms after pods warm up. No customer 5xx. I'll mark PD alert as acknowledged and add notes.

pagerduty-bot: :white_check_mark: Alert P12345 acknowledged by tyler (on-call).

tyler (on-call): updating incident timeline in the runbook and creating a follow-up ticket: infra#3421 - investigate kv-cache prefetch + quant kernel fallback; assign sam.

sam (eng-runtime): noted. I'll reproduce locally with batch traces and add guard + a unit perf test.

jamie (product): I'll draft a short customer-facing blurb explaining we saw elevated embedding latency during a canary rollout, mitigated by rollback; no data loss. Please add any org-ids impacted to the support ticket.

maria (eng-sre): closing the active on-call rotation for this thread. If anything resurfaces, re-open PD.

tyler (on-call): handing off to @rachael for post-incident monitoring and follow-up. Rachael, can you keep watch for the next 2h and ping if p95 > 250ms?

rachael (next-oncall): taking watch. I added a dashboard alert for p95 > 250ms and a slack webhook to this channel.

tyler (on-call): thanks all. Summary: canary v3.4.0 caused quant-kernel fallback on embedding shard -> latency spike; mitigation: traffic-set to 0% then rollback, metrics returned to normal. Follow-up ticket infra#3421 assigned to sam.

incident-bot: :page_with_curl: Incident created: INC-2026-0314-emb-latency. Timeline and runbook link: https://redwood.example/incidents/INC-2026-0314-emb-latency

rachael (next-oncall): acknowledged, I'll take postmortem and link to infra ticket when it's ready.

jamie (product): grateful for the quick response. I'll coordinate comms with support. :thumbsup:

(threads ends)
